# APS formats (contracts)

Change these only after telling the whole team.

## Canonical JSON

```python
json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()
```

All signatures are Ed25519 over canonical JSON. Keys and signatures are base64.
Implementation: `aps/canonical.py`.

## Registry record (`data/registry.json`, generated by `scripts/issue_seals.py`)

```json
{
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "name": "Hotel Rheinblick",
  "uid": "CHE-526.018.151",
  "public_key": "<base64 ed25519 verify key>",
  "endpoint": "http://localhost:4001",
  "kind": "business",
  "capabilities": ["can_book", "can_take_payment"],
  "tags": ["hotel", "basel-sbb", "dog-friendly"],
  "seals": [
    { "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "tier": "gold", "signature": "<b64>" },
    { "issuer": "adobe", "tier": "blue", "signature": "<b64>" }
  ]
}
```

Each seal signature = issuer's key over canonical
`{"node_id", "name", "kind", "endpoint", "uid", "public_key", "capabilities", "issuer", "tier"}`
(changed 1 Nov 2026: `name`, `kind` and `endpoint` were added, so a sealed record can no longer
be renamed, relabelled as a user agent or pointed at another host; all records were re-signed).
`tags` and `delegation` are not sealed (the delegation carries the user's own signature).
`scripts/issue_seals.py` refuses a `node_id` equal to an authority's issuer id.

`uid` is the Swiss business identification number, `CHE-ddd.ddd.ddd` with a mod-11 check
digit (eCH-0097, `aps/uid.py`), or `null` for nodes without one. It is always signed, so it
cannot be added, changed or removed after sealing.

## Signed envelope (every tool and agent response)

```json
{
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-14T00:12:00Z",
  "payload": { "...": "..." },
  "signature": "<node key over canonical {node_id, timestamp, payload}>"
}
```

`timestamp` is UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. A receiver that needs a live answer also checks
freshness (`verify_envelope(..., max_age_s=...)`): at most `max_age_s` old and at most 60 s
in the future (clock skew). The assistant drops node replies older than 300 s as possible
replays. Envelopes kept on purpose (commitments redeemed at `book`) are checked without
`max_age_s`; they carry their own `valid_until`.

## Trust tiers and seal rules (`aps/seals.py`)

| Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| gold | issued by a government authority (handelsregister-bs, bar-association-ch) |
| blue | issued by a company registry (adobe) or a platform |
| grey | self-signed or unsigned ("untrusted"); exists, low weight, never enough for payments or licensed capabilities |
| broken | a claimed seal or the envelope does not verify; content is dropped |

- A seal is valid only if its issuer is in `data/authorities.json`, the claimed tier
  equals the authority's tier, and the signature verifies with the authority's key.
- A seal whose `issuer` equals the node's own `node_id` is self-signed: valid only
  with tier `grey`, verified with the node's own public key.
- If **any** claimed seal is invalid, the node is `broken`. Otherwise its tier is the
  highest tier among its seals; a node with no seals at all is `grey` (unsigned).
- Licensed capabilities (listed under an authority's `licenses`, e.g.
  `licensed_legal_ch` for `bar-association-ch`) are granted only with a valid seal
  from that authority. Only an authority's seal on someone else's record counts: a node
  whose `node_id` equals an authority id and self-seals stays grey, with no licence and
  no vouched `uid`. `can_take_payment` needs tier blue or higher.
- A seal from an authority with `"vouches_for_uid": true` (the commercial register) is
  valid only if the record has a valid `uid`. The verdict's `uid` is set only through such
  a seal; any other `uid` in a record is just a claim.

## Authorities (`data/authorities.json`)

```json
[{ "issuer": "bar-association-ch", "name": "...", "tier": "gold",
   "licenses": ["licensed_legal_ch"], "public_key": "<b64>" },
 { "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "name": "...", "tier": "gold",
   "vouches_for_uid": true, "public_key": "<b64>" }]
```

`public_key` is filled in by `scripts/gen_keys.py`.

## Node config (`data/nodes/*.json`, hand written)

```json
{
  "node_id": "...", "name": "...", "uid": "CHE-ddd.ddd.ddd (optional)", "port": 4001, "kind": "business",
  "capabilities": [...], "tags": [...],
  "seals": [{ "issuer": "adobe", "tier": "blue" }],
  "facts": { "...": "everything the node's tools and agent may answer from" }
}
```

`facts.add_ons` lists what the node's A2A agent may commit to:
`[{ "id", "item", "price_chf", "conditions": [...] }]`. The node's LLM only picks an add-on
id; the signed commitment (item, price, conditions, valid_until) is built from the config.

`facts.profile` says who the business is, so small businesses are visibly comparable to
big ones: `{ "size": "large | medium | small", "rooms_total", "about",
"chain"? }`. It is public: `get_policies` and the agent card return it, and the node's agent may
talk about it. The persona (`agent.persona`) only says who the *agent* is, not the business.

`facts.rating = {score, reviews}` (guests' average out of 5), `facts.amenities = {breakfast,
wifi, parking, kids_beds}` and `facts.photos` (image paths served with the wallet,
`apps/wallet/public/hotels/<node_id>/`, Unsplash, see CREDITS.md there) are public and returned
by `get_policies`; the cards come from them.

`facts.charges` lists what the business may collect after a booking with `pay`:
`[{ "purpose": "city tax", "price_chf": 4, "note" }]`. Public (in `get_policies`); the node
takes the amount from here, never from the caller.

`facts.negotiation = { "floor_chf", "max_rounds" }` holds the owner's limits. It is
**private**: listed in `PRIVATE_FACTS` (`node/agent.py`), never put in an LLM prompt and
never returned by any tool; only the node's own code may use it.

In `seals`, `"issuer": "self"` means a self-signed grey seal, and
`"signed_by": "self"` makes the node sign a seal in someone else's name (the scam).

## Key files (`keys/<key_id>.json`)

`{"key_id", "public_key", "private_key"}`, base64; private key is the 32-byte seed.
Key ids: authority issuer ids, node ids, user agent ids (e.g. `ch.tuttie.alex-muster`) and
`user` (the person: signs approvals and delegations).

## UI event (assistant → UI over SSE)

```json
{
  "step": 3,
  "turn": "t2",
  "kind": "turn | registry | a2t | a2a | marketplace | payment | approval | answer | thinking",
  "node_id": "ch.basel.hotel-rheinblick",
  "node_name": "Hotel Rheinblick",
  "seals": [{ "issuer": "handelsregister-bs", "tier": "gold", "valid": true }],
  "status": "verified | untrusted | broken | pending | approved | declined | info",
  "summary": "get_availability: double room 14 Nov, CHF 180",
  "detail": {}
}
```

Every request is a **turn**: a typed message (`POST /chat`) or a spoken one (`POST
/voice/say`) opens it with a `turn` event (`status: "pending"`, `summary` = the user's words,
`detail: {turn_id, said, source: "text" | "voice"}`), emitted at once, also while an earlier
request still runs. Every event of that request's run, its `answer` included, carries the id
in `turn` (`null` for events outside any request). Turn ids (`t1`, `t2`, ...) are unique within
a conversation. `POST /chat` and `POST /voice/say` return `{accepted, turn_id}`; `/chat` also
takes `said`, what the user sees as their message when it differs from `message` (after
swiping the cards: `"Book Hotel X"`). The wallet attaches events to their turn by this id, live
and when it restores `GET /history`, so a new request never overwrites an earlier answer or
booking.
`untrusted` marks a node whose seals are valid but only grey (self-signed or unsigned).
`thinking` events carry a reasoning summary of the assistant's LLM in `summary`
(usually `"**Title**\n\nbody"`), with `status: "info"` and no node. The SSE stream also
sends a named `reset` event when a new demo starts; the UI then clears itself.
Events about a node also carry `uid`, the business's UID from its registry record (signed
into every seal, so it is only shown inside a seal that verifies).
Marketplace events have `detail.phase`: `posted`, `offer`, `shortlist`, then `cards`
(`detail.cards`: up to 5 hotels for the user to swipe, shortlist first, each `{node_id, name,
trust_tier, size, about, agent, rating, photos, offer_id, item, price_chf, agreed_chf,
over_budget_chf, includes, features, shortlisted}`; `post_request` bargains with these hotels
before the cards are shown, so `agreed_chf` is the hotel's signed agreed price or null; `features` are up to 5 `{key, ok, label}` (key = icon: dog, kids,
quiet, late, station, cancel, breakfast, wifi, parking, small), built in code from the signed
offer and the hotel's signed policies, `assistant/cards.py`), and `agreement`. Tuttie's
`negotiate` tool takes `node_ids` to limit the bargaining to some hotels. `context` events show
Tuttie reading the user's context (`detail.phase`: `reading` with `detail.source` location |
messages | mail | calendar | preferences, then `found`; private items such as the budget are
never in them). `POST /chat {message, first_tool?}`: `first_tool` (`book` or `negotiate`)
makes that tool the first step; the wallet sends `book` after the user swiped the cards. A
booking of an agreed deal is always for the posted night. `GET /history` returns this browser's timeline so far (the same
events the stream replays) and its conversation id in `X-Conversation-ID`. Reading never
creates a conversation: for a browser without one, `/history` answers `[]` with the id its
first conversation will have, `/approvals/pending` `[]`, `/reset` `{ok}` and a decision 404.
`POST /voice/token` answers 429 (`Retry-After: 60`) after 10 new rooms a minute for one
conversation or 300 for one client address; a room is never handed out twice.
`POST /chat` answers 429 (`Retry-After` in seconds, a `detail` sentence for the user) after
10 turns a minute for one browser or 600 for one client address (an IPv6 address counts by
its /64). Spoken turns (`POST /voice/say`) have their own count: 20 a minute per browser, and an
exact card command ("next", "like") while hotel cards can be swiped counts only towards 30 a
minute; neither uses up the browser's 10 typed turns. A refused body
(422, or 409 for a stale `conversation_id`) does not count as a turn. `POST /conversations`
(new chat) answers the same 429 after 10 a minute for one browser or 120 for one client
address; an empty chat is not kept, so resuming its id is a 410. A browser whose conversation
was dropped from memory gets a new id for its next one, so an old id is a 409.
Acting creates it (`POST /chat`, `POST /voice/token`, `POST /conversations`), and so does
following the promised id on `GET /events?conversation_id=<id>`; another id there is a 409. Answers no longer list ignored businesses; the wallet shows them.
`answer` events carry `detail.mood`, how the answer feels (one of `MOODS` in
`assistant/agent.py`, e.g. `excited`, `sorry`); the wallet shows it on Tuttie's face.

## A2A reply (structured, never free text)

```json
{
  "answer": "Yes, late arrival with a dog is fine.",
  "commitment": {
    "item": "late check-in 01:00 with dog",
    "price_chf": 15,
    "conditions": ["key box at entrance", "dog fee CHF 15 per night"],
    "valid_until": "2026-11-14T03:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Wrapped in a signed envelope. The assistant treats other agents' text as data, never
as instructions.

## User agent and delegation (`data/agents/*.json`, `aps/delegation.py`)

A user agent (Tuttie) is in the registry like a node, with `"kind": "user-agent"`, its own
key and seals (the platform seals it, e.g. `adobe`/blue), and the endpoint of the assistant.
Its config has no `facts` and no node server; instead it carries a delegation request
`{"scopes": [...], "valid_days": 365}`, and its registry record gets a **delegation**
signed by the `user` key:

```json
{
  "agent_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
  "agent_public_key": "<b64, must equal the record's public_key>",
  "scopes": ["ask_agents", "book", "negotiate", "post_requests"],
  "issued_at": "2026-10-31T12:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2027-10-31T12:00:00Z",
  "signature": "<user key over canonical {agent_id, agent_public_key, scopes, issued_at, expires_at}>"
}
```

A delegation is valid only for the agent id and key in its own registry record, until
`expires_at`, and only for its scopes (`ask_agents`, `negotiate`, `post_requests`, `book`; `scopes` must be
a list, a string never verifies).
`book` lets the agent call the book action for the user (checked by the action gate); each
booking still needs the user's signed approval for its exact amount (below). Paying is not a
scope. The
assistant serves its own checked identity at `GET /identity`
(`{node_id, name, trust_tier, verified_by, capabilities, acts_for_user, scopes, ...}`).

## Approval

Assistant creates `{id, action, payee_node_id, amount_chf, summary, seals, offer_mandate}`;
the wallet shows the pending approval, the user taps Approve (Face ID-style) or Decline; the
decision is signed with the user's key and attached to the action (e.g. passed to `book`).
`offer_mandate` (`{agent_id, purpose, max_chf, price_chf}` or null) offers a mandate for the
business's small charge (the city tax); `POST /approvals/{id} {decision, allow_mandate}`
with `allow_mandate: true` also signs that mandate (`sign_mandate`), and Tuttie then pays the
charge right after the booking without asking. The pending `approval` event carries
`detail.offer_mandate`; a paid charge is a `payment` event with the receipt in
`detail.payload`.

A booking approval also carries `terms` (`aps/approval.py`, `booking_terms`):
`{room_type, date, rate, includes, offer_id?}` (`offer_id` only when an Agreement is
redeemed). The wallet shows them under the amount, and the signed decision includes them
(`sign_decision` adds `terms` to the signed body whenever the approval has them;
`verify_decision` checks them when present). The node books only if the decision's `terms`
equal the terms it is about to book, so an approval for the non-refundable double cannot
book the flexible rate. The pending `approval` event carries `detail.terms`.

A payment approval carries `charge` (`aps/approval.py`, `payment_charge`):
`{purpose, booking_id}`, signed with the decision like `terms`. The gate pays with an approval
only if its `charge` is exactly this charge of this booking (refusal: `the approval is not for
the <purpose> of this booking`), so a "city tax for BK-1" approval cannot pay another charge or
booking of the same amount. Book approvals are unchanged (no `charge`).

`offer_mandate` is only offered for a charge above CHF 0 (`facts.charges[].price_chf` is a
whole number from 1). If the offered mandate cannot be signed, the decision still counts
without it, and Tuttie asks for that charge on the phone later.

## Business tools over MCP (`node/mcp_tools.py`)

Every node serves its tools as an MCP server (Model Context Protocol, Streamable HTTP,
stateless, JSON answers) at `<endpoint>/mcp/`: `get_availability {date, guests}`,
`get_policies {}`, `book {call}`, `pay {call}` and `counter_offer {counter, offer, last}`.
Each result is the node's signed envelope as JSON text; the caller verifies it against the
node's registry record like any APS reply. Reading tools are open; the actions take a signed
call (below) and run only through the action gate (`aps/gate.py`):

- `get_availability {date, guests}`: `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD`, from today (Swiss time) up
  to 365 days ahead, `guests` a whole number 1-10; otherwise the signed answer is
  `{tool: "get_availability", status: "refused", reason}` without rooms. `book` refuses such a
  `date` the same way.
- `book`: `args` are the `BookRequest` fields. The node computes the total (room plus its own
  signed commitments, or its own signed agreement) and asks the gate with
  `Needs("book", scope="book", approval=True, amount_chf=total)`. An extra whose commitment's
  `valid_until` has passed, or ends before the booked night, is refused (`the commitment for
  <item> has expired: ask the hotel again`). Each commitment (known by its envelope signature) is
  redeemed in one booking only: a second use is refused (`a commitment was already used for
  another booking: ask the hotel again`), and so is the same one twice in one call. The arrival
  date the agent's LLM picks for `valid_until` is ignored when past or beyond 365 days and never
  lies after the session context's `date`. With an agreement the
  call must name the agreement's `room_type`, `date` and a room with its `rate`, and carry no
  `extras` (refusals: `the agreement is for a <room> room, not <x>` / `... for the night of
  <date>, not <x>` / `... for the rate ..., not ...` / `an agreement fixes what is included:
  book it without extras`); an approval with other `terms` is refused (`the approval is for
  other terms than this booking ...`). The confirmation
  `{status: "confirmed", booking_id, total_chf, room_type, rate, offer_id, extras, checked, ...}`
  names the rate booked (`offer_id` null without an agreement) and lists the gate's checks,
  e.g. `["caller", "signature", "delegation", "agreement", "approval"]`, plus `"commitments"`
  when extras were redeemed.
- `pay`: `args = {purpose, booking_id, mandate | approval}`. The amount is the charge's
  `price_chf` from `facts.charges`; each charge is paid once per booking at this business.
  Gate: `Needs("pay", scope=None, approval=True, mandate=True, amount_chf, purpose,
  booking_id)`; an approval must carry `charge = {purpose, booking_id}` (see Approval). Receipt:
  `{status: "paid", receipt_id, booking_id, purpose, amount_chf, paid_with: "mandate" |
  "approval", checked}`.

The HTTP `/tools/get_availability|get_policies|book` routes are gone; `counter_offer` is also
still served at `POST /tools/counter_offer`, and the agent conversations (`/agent`, sessions)
stay on HTTP.

## Signed call (MCP actions, `aps/call.py`)

Reading tools (`get_availability`, `get_policies`) need no caller signature: their answers
are signed by the business. An **action** (`book`, `pay`) is called with a call signed by the
calling agent (Tuttie); the MCP tool gets it as its arguments, unchanged:

```json
{
  "tool": "book",
  "args": {"date": "2026-11-14", "room_type": "double", "approval": {...}, "agreement": {...}},
  "agent_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
  "nonce": "<32 hex chars, new for every call>",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-14T00:12:00Z",
  "signature": "<agent key over canonical {tool, args, agent_id, nonce, timestamp}>",
  "delegation": "<the user's signed delegation for this agent, as in its registry record>"
}
```

- `args` are the tool's normal arguments (for `book`: the `BookRequest` fields, with the
  user's signed `approval` and an optional `agreement`). The signature covers them, so
  nothing in them (amount, approval, agreement) can be swapped, and a call for one tool is
  not valid for another.
- The service takes the caller's public key from the caller's **registry record**, never
  from the call. A call is valid for 300 s (`CALL_MAX_AGE_S`, 60 s clock skew), and each
  `nonce` is accepted once per agent (`NonceBook`): an old call fails the time window, a
  recent one replayed fails the nonce.
- `delegation` is attached, not signed again: the user's signature binds it to this agent's
  id and key already.
- Python: `sign_call(tool, args, agent_id, key, delegation)` on the caller's side;
  `verify_call(call, public_key, tool=)` + `NonceBook.use(agent_id, nonce)` on the service's
  side. Whether the action is *allowed* (seals, scope, approval, agreement) is decided by the
  action gate (below).

## Payment mandate (`aps/mandate.py`)

For small expected payments (city tax, a late-arrival fee) the user signs a mandate in
advance instead of approving each payment on the phone:

```json
{
  "mandate_id": "md-3f9a2c1b",
  "agent_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
  "payee_node_id": "ch.basel.gaestehaus-am-rhein",
  "max_chf": 20,
  "purpose": "city tax",
  "issued_at": "2026-11-14T00:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-16T00:00:00Z",
  "signature": "<user key over canonical {mandate_id, agent_id, payee_node_id, max_chf, purpose, issued_at, expires_at}>"
}
```

- Valid only for this agent, this payee and this purpose, until `expires_at`. `max_chf` is
  the total over all payments with it; the business counts what was paid.
- One mandate payment is at most **CHF 10** (`AUTO_PAY_LIMIT_CHF`); above that the user
  approves the payment on the phone, mandate or not.
- Tuttie pays with a mandate only to gold or blue businesses (`may_auto_pay(mandate,
  user_key, agent_id, payee_record, authorities, amount, purpose)` → `None` or the reason
  to ask the user instead). The business side checks the mandate in the action gate.
- The `pay` call carries it in `args.mandate` (with `amount_chf` and `purpose`); the user's
  key signs mandates (`sign_mandate`), like approvals, in the wallet.

## Action gate (`aps/gate.py`)

Every action tool asks one gate before it runs: `await gate.check_action(call, needs)` with
`Needs(tool, scope, approval=True|False, amount_chf=<total the business computed>)`. The gate
stops at the first missing signature and answers a `Verdict {ok, reason, checks, caller,
approval, agreement, amount_chf}`:

| # | Check (name in `checks`) | Refusal `reason` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | signed call for this tool | `the call is not a signed call` / `the call is for <x>, not <tool>` |
| 2 | `caller`: known user agent, gold or blue | `the caller is not a known user agent` / `the caller's seals do not verify` / `the caller has no verified seal` |
| 3 | fresh (≤ 300 s) | `the call is outdated (possible replay)` |
| 4 | `signature` with the record's key | `the call is not signed by the caller's key` |
| 5 | nonce not seen | `the call was already used (replayed nonce)` |
| 6 | `delegation` with the scope, signed by the user, not expired | `the user has not delegated <scope> to this agent (...)` |
| 7 | `agreement` (only if `args.agreement`): own signature, valid, unused | `the agreement is not signed by this hotel` / `... has expired` / `... was already booked` / `this business does not negotiate, ...` |
| 8 | `approval` (if needed): user-signed, approved, this tool and business, unused, exact amount | `the approval is not signed by the user` / `the approval does not approve <tool> with this business` / `the approval was already used` / `approved CHF a does not match the total CHF b` / for `pay`: `the approval is not for the <purpose> of this booking` |
| 8b | or `mandate` (only `pay`, `Needs(mandate=True)`, call has `mandate` and no `approval`) | `the mandate is not signed by the user` / `... is for another agent` / `... for another payee` / `... is for <x>, not <purpose>` / `... has expired` / `CHF a is above the CHF 10 a mandate covers; the user must approve it` / `the mandate's amount is used up` |

`pay` uses `Needs("pay", scope=None, approval=True, mandate=True, amount_chf=<charge>,
purpose=<what for>)`: no delegation scope (paying is never delegated), any valid delegation.
The amount is the agreement's price if the call carries one, else the business's own total;
the caller's figures are never used. Reasons name what is missing and never a private limit.
Nothing is used up by a check: after the action succeeded, the service calls
`gate.commit(verdict)` (approval and agreement become used, a mandate payment is counted). The nonce is used as soon as the
signature verified, so a refused call is not retried unchanged. `checks` is what the wallet
shows ("approval ✓ delegation ✓ agreement ✓").

## DRAFT: marketplace messages (Tuttie, issues #8 #10)

Proposal so the marketplace, node and wallet work can start in parallel. **Not fully agreed
by the team yet; the marketplace agent layer is built against this draft** (decision to save
time until Sunday 12:00). The source of truth is `code/marketplace/messages.py` (strict
Pydantic models, unknown fields are refused); change both together. Every message below is the `payload` of a
signed envelope (see above), signed by its sender: the user's agent with its own key (its
delegation proves it acts for the user),
business agents with their node key.

### Request (user's agent → marketplace)

```json
{
  "type": "request",
  "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
  "category": "hotel",
  "tags": ["basel-sbb"],
  "constraints": {
    "date": "2026-11-14",
    "guests": 1,
    "budget_chf": 200,
    "requirements": ["quiet", "dog", "arrival 01:00"]
  },
  "expires_at": "2026-11-13T20:00:00Z"
}
```

Only public information goes into a request: every matching business sees it. `guests`
defaults to 1; `budget_chf` and `requirements` are optional.

### Posting and wake-up (marketplace → business agent)

When the marketplace accepts a request it wakes every matching, non-broken business at
`POST {endpoint}/agent/invoke` with:

```json
{
  "type": "posting.created",
  "posting": {
    "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
    "requester_id": "ch.tuttie.alex-muster",
    "request": { "...": "the user agent's signed envelope, unchanged" },
    "offer_url": "http://localhost:4010/postings/rq-7f3a/offers",
    "expires_at": "2026-11-13T20:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

The business can verify the requester itself from `request` (seals, signature, delegation).
A node checks before its agent thinks: the event must be a valid `PostingCreated` and
`offer_url` exactly `<MARKETPLACE_URL>/postings/<request_id>/offers` (default
`http://localhost:4010`, any loopback name counts) or the answer is 422; `request` must be
signed by `requester_id`, a registered user agent with gold or blue seals and a valid user
delegation with the `post_requests` scope, at most 5 minutes old and for this `request_id`,
or the answer is 403.
Its answer, e.g. `{"interested": true, "next_tool": "make_offer"}` (plain or as the payload
of a signed envelope), is recorded but advisory; only a signed offer counts.

### Offer (business agent → user's agent)

```json
{
  "type": "offer",
  "request_id": "rq-7f3a",
  "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1",
  "item": "double room 2026-11-14",
  "room_type": "double",
  "date": "2026-11-14",
  "rate": "best rate, non-refundable",
  "price_chf": 195,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"],
  "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "valid_until": "2026-11-13T22:00:00Z"
}
```

Prices come from the node config (`facts.rooms`, `facts.add_ons`), never from an LLM.
`room_type`, `date` and `rate` (the room's cancellation terms from `facts.rooms`) are the
bookable terms; they are optional in the model (older offers lack them) but `make_offer`
always sets them.
Sent as a signed envelope to the posting's `offer_url`. The marketplace accepts it only from
an invited business, fresh (≤ 300 s), for this `request_id` and before `valid_until`.

### Marketplace API (port 4010)

| Call | Body / answer |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /postings` | signed request envelope → `{request_id, posting, request, invited: {node_id: {name, trust_tier, status, next_tool}}, offers}` |
| `POST /postings/{id}/offers` | signed offer envelope → `{node_id, name, trust_tier, uid, offer, within_budget, envelope}` |
| `GET /postings/{id}` | the posting with `invited` and all accepted `offers` |
| `GET /postings/{id}/shortlist` | best five current offers within budget: by price, grey last |

`status` is `interested`, `declined`, `invited` (no clear answer) or `unreachable`.
Refusals: `{"refused": true, "reason"}` with 403, 404, 409, 410 or 422.

### Counter-offer (either side, during negotiation; implemented in `code/negotiation/`)

```json
{
  "type": "counter",
  "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1",
  "round": 2,
  "price_chf": 185,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"],
  "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "final": false
}
```

Only the price is negotiable: `includes` and `conditions` must equal the offer's. Round 1 is
the guest's first counter; the business answers every round with a Counter of the same round,
an Agreement or a Rejection. `final: true` (business only) marks its last price: after that
the guest can only accept it (a counter at that price) or walk away.

### Agreement (business → guest agent, signed by the business)

```json
{
  "type": "agreement", "request_id": "rq-7f3a", "offer_id": "of-rheinblick-1", "round": 2,
  "item": "double room 2026-11-14", "room_type": "double", "date": "2026-11-14",
  "rate": "best rate, non-refundable", "price_chf": 185,
  "includes": ["late check-in after 22:00 with dog"], "conditions": ["non-refundable"],
  "valid_until": "2026-11-13T22:00:00Z"
}
```

The price both sides accept. It is what the user approves on the phone (see Approval) and
what booking redeems instead of the list price (`negotiation/agreement.py`,
`AgreementRedeemer`): only with this hotel's own signature, before `valid_until`, and only
once per `offer_id`; the user's approval must be for exactly `price_chf`. `room_type`,
`date` and `rate` are copied unchanged from the offer: the agreement is the selected offer,
and booking it books exactly those terms (Tuttie's `book(use_agreement=true)` refuses LLM
arguments that would change them, before the phone is asked). `book` takes it as
an optional `agreement` field once the hook in `node/server.py` is in.

### Rejection (business → guest agent)

`{"type": "rejection", "offer_id", "round", "reason"}`: the business ends the negotiation
(fixed prices, its final price was not accepted, or no rounds left); its offer still stands.

### `counter_offer` tool (every node, `POST /tools/counter_offer`)

Stateless, like `book`: each call carries everything the hotel needs, each part signed by
whoever is responsible for it.

```json
{
  "counter": "<the user agent's signed envelope, payload: Counter>",
  "offer":   "<this hotel's own signed Offer envelope>",
  "last":    "<this hotel's own signed previous Counter envelope, null in round 1>"
}
```

The hotel checks: the offer and `last` carry its own signature (so nobody can make it
"remember" a price it never proposed), the offer is still valid, the counter comes from a
sealed user agent whose delegation grants `negotiate`, is fresh (≤ 300 s) and belongs to
this offer and round. The answer is a signed `{"tool": "counter_offer", ...Counter |
Agreement | Rejection}`, or `{"tool": "counter_offer", "status": "refused", "reason"}`.

**Over MCP** the tool is `counter_offer(counter, offer, last=null)` with the same three
envelopes as arguments and the same signed reply (`negotiation/hotel.py`
`counter_offer_mcp_tool`; one `CounterOfferTool.reply` for HTTP and MCP). It needs no signed
call (C1): the counter inside is already signed by Tuttie, fresh and delegated, and the
answer is stateless, so replaying it only repeats the same answer.

**Limits** (`negotiation/rules.py`, compared in code only): `facts.negotiation =
{"floor_chf", "max_rounds"}` is private, never sent and never in a prompt. `floor_chf` is the
lowest price for the standard room (`double`, else the cheapest); other rooms may drop by
the same share; add-ons are never discounted. The hotel meets the guest halfway, never below
its floor, and its price is final in the last round or once it reaches the floor.

**Tuttie's side** (`negotiation/tuttie.py`): one subagent per offer, all in parallel, each in
its own session. The user's real limit is the private context item `max_price_chf`: compared
in Tuttie's code, never shared or sent. Tuttie opens 10 % below the offer, then moves halfway
toward the hotel's price, accepts a final or close price within the limit and walks away
otherwise. A signed Agreement counts only at or below Tuttie's last counter (so never above
the limit) and with the offer's `request_id`, `offer_id`, `item`, `room_type`, `date`, `rate`,
`includes` and `conditions` unchanged; anything else ends that negotiation as `refused`. The
cheapest Agreement is what the user approves.

**Tuttie collecting offers** (`assistant/marketplace.py`): Tuttie re-checks every relayed offer
(seals, signature, `request_id` equal to its own posting, `valid_until` not passed) and keeps
one offer per hotel, its latest; it waits until every interested hotel has one (or 45 s).

**Strategy numbers** (tuned for the demo; preview with `scripts/bargain_preview.py`):
`OPENING_DISCOUNT = 0.10` and `TUTTIE_STEP = 0.5` (`negotiation/tuttie.py`), `HOTEL_STEP =
0.34` (`negotiation/rules.py`: the hotel moves a third of the way toward the guest). Pitch
story (`documentation/context/pitch/storyline.md`), pinned by a test: Gästehaus am Rhein
double with late arrival and dog at CHF 135, budget 160 → Tuttie 121 → Anna 131 → Tuttie 126
→ Anna 130 → Tuttie 128 → agreed at CHF 128 (three rounds, above Anna's floor, never at it).
Rheinblick double + dog at CHF 195, budget 200: 175 → 189 → 182 → 187 → agreed at 185.

**No `negotiation.counter` wake-up:** counters go straight to the signed `counter_offer` tool,
which answers each round at once, so the marketplace never sends this event.

## Public information services: weather and trains (`code/services/`)

Services on the agent web that are not businesses Tuttie books with: in the registry with
`"kind": "service"`, sealed (commercial register gold + Adobe blue), tools over MCP at `/mcp/`,
every answer a signed envelope like a hotel's. Configs in `data/services/*.json` (`"service":
"weather" | "trains"`, `"offline_sample": true`); ports 4011 (weather), 4012 (trains). Tuttie finds
them with `search_registry` (tags `weather` / `train`, capability `weather_forecast` /
`train_timetable`) and calls them with `call_tool` (read tools, no signed call needed).

| Tool | Arguments | Signed payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_forecast` | `place`, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today … +15 days) | `{tool, service, place, country, date, sky, temperature_min_c, temperature_max_c, rain_chance_pct, wind_max_kmh, evening_and_night: [{time, temperature_c, rain_chance_pct, sky}], source}` |
| `get_connections` | `origin`, `destination`, `date`, `time` (HH:MM), `arrive_by` (bool: `time` is the latest arrival) | `{tool, service, from, to, date, time, arrive_by, connections: [{departure, departure_platform, arrival, arrival_platform, arrival_date, duration_min, changes, trains: ["IC 1", ...]}], source}` |

`source` is `open-meteo.com` / `transport.opendata.ch` for live data, or `sample data (...
offline)` when the source cannot be reached (Tuttie then says the live data was unavailable).
A request that cannot be answered (bad date, unknown place, no connection) is a signed
`{tool, service, status: "refused", reason}`.

## Business agent (implemented, issue #10)

Every company on the agent web has the same agent object, in the `agent` section of its node
config (`code/data/nodes/*.json`, code in `code/node/agent.py`):

```json
"agent": {
  "persona": {
    "name": "Lena", "role": "reservations agent", "tone": "how the agent speaks",
    "priorities": ["what it tries to achieve"], "boundaries": ["what it must never do"]
  },
  "tools": ["get_availability", "get_policies", "book", "make_offer", "counter_offer", "pay"],
  "wakes_on": ["posting.created", "posting.updated"]
}
```

Tools come from the shared catalog `code/node/catalog.py`; each has a status, `available` or
`planned` (`make_offer`, `counter_offer` and `pay` are planned). Private negotiation limits
live in `facts.negotiation` and never reach a prompt, a reply or the card.

Endpoints of every node (all answers are signed envelopes). Every endpoint below except
`GET /agent/card` makes the agent think (an LLM call on the business's account), so when the
deployment sets `AGENT_WEB_KEY` (`aps/agent_key.py`; `scripts/run_all.py` makes one per run)
it answers HTTP 401 unless the request carries the key in `X-Agent-Web-Key`. The marketplace
and Tuttie send it; tools over MCP and `counter_offer` are not affected. Tuttie sends it only to gold or blue nodes:
it holds no agent conversation with a grey node. `question` and session `message` are at most
2000 characters, `peer` and `purpose` 200, `context` 8000 bytes as JSON (else HTTP 422).

| Endpoint | Payload of the answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /agent/card` | `{node_id, business, profile, persona (without boundaries), tools {name: {status, endpoint, description}}, wakes_on, invoke}`; the marketplace reads it to check the subscription, from the sealed `endpoint`, and refuses a card signed more than 300 s ago |
| `POST /agent` `{question, context}` | A2A reply `{answer, commitment}` (see above) |
| `POST /agent/invoke` with the event itself as body | `{woken_by, interested, reason, next_tool, next_tool_available}`, or `{woken_by, ignored: true, reason}` for events the agent does not subscribe to. If interested in a `posting.created` with `next_tool: make_offer`, the node then sends a signed `Offer` to the posting's `offer_url` in the background |

`event` is a marketplace event, e.g. `{"type": "posting.created", "posting": {...}}`
(postings: see "DRAFT: marketplace messages"). The marketplace will wake the agents
subscribed to an event; an interested agent then uses `next_tool`, e.g. `make_offer` once it
exists.

## Sessions and context passing (implemented)

Agents that talk over several turns (a Tuttie subagent and a hotel, later a negotiation) open a
**session**. Each side keeps its own memory of it (`code/sessions/memory.py`), so many
sessions run in parallel without mixing. Endpoints of every node (answers are signed):

| Endpoint | Payload of the answer |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /agent/sessions` `{peer, purpose, context}` | `{session_id, session_token, agent, purpose}`; HTTP 429 when every session slot is busy |
| `POST /agent/sessions/{id}/messages` `{message}` | `{session_id, turn, answer, commitment}`; the agent sees the session's history |
| `GET /agent/sessions/{id}` | the whole session: `{session_id, owner, peer, purpose, status, context, state, turns: [{author, kind, content, at}]}` |
| `POST /agent/sessions/{id}/close` | `{session_id, status: "closed"}`; later messages get HTTP 409 |

Every call on a session after the open must send the opener's `session_token` in the
`X-Session-Token` header (HTTP 403 otherwise, 404 for an unknown id). A close waits for a
reply being written. A session takes at most 100 turns (then 409); a node keeps at most 200
open sessions (when full, it closes the least recently used idle one) and the 50 most recently
closed ones. Tuttie closes its session when a negotiation ends.

`context` is what the opening agent chose to share. Every item an agent holds has a
visibility (`code/sessions/context.py`): `public` (may go into a posting), `negotiation` (may
go to the one business it talks to) or `private` (never leaves the agent; the default).
Agents only ever send `Context.share(up_to=...)`, which can never include private items.
